content.content:
-- A project can be marked ACTIVE, ON_HOLD or FINISHED so its state is visible on the list. Additive
-- column with a default, so existing rows and any caller that omits it start ACTIVE. The CHECK pins
-- the column to the three known values, mirroring the other value-guard migrations.
ALTER TABLE project ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ACTIVE';
ALTER TABLE project ADD CONSTRAINT project_status_valid
    CHECK (status IN ('ACTIVE', 'ON_HOLD', 'FINISHED'));
---V3---
-- Second domain table: projects the user does for a client. Each project has a name and belongs to
-- exactly one client (client_id FK). IDENTITY id like client, so the DB assigns it on insert while
-- the seed path can still supply explicit ids (GENERATED BY DEFAULT).
CREATE TABLE project (
    id        BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    client_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES client(id)
);
---V16---
-- Archiving a project tucks it away instead of deleting it: the row is kept but drops off the
-- default lists. A boolean flag on project, defaulting FALSE so every existing (and newly created)
-- project starts un-archived and visible.
ALTER TABLE project ADD COLUMN archived BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE;

The test passes. 

The change was small because the schema (`V21__project_status.sql`), server (`ProjectsGet`/`ProjectView` returning `status`), and seed support were already in place. I added the missing filter:

1. **`features/projects/statusFilter.slot.tsx`** (new file) — a `project-status-filter` `<select>` filling the projects toolbar slot (order 30), owning the `projectStatus` URL search-param key. Empty option clears the filter.
